speeches.text: A Norman.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Upon my life, Lamord.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: The very same.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: I know him well. He is the brooch indeed And gem of all the nation.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: He made confession of you And gave you such a masterly report For art and exercise in your defense, And for your rapier most especial, That he cried out ’twould be a sight indeed If one could match you. The ’scrimers of their nation He swore had neither motion, guard, nor eye, If you opposed them. Sir, this report of his Did Hamlet so envenom with his envy That he could nothing do but wish and beg Your sudden coming-o’er, to play with you. Now out of this—

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: What out of this, my lord?

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Laertes, was your father dear to you? Or are you like the painting of a sorrow, A face without a heart?

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Why ask you this?

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Not that I think you did not love your father, But that I know love is begun by time And that I see, in passages of proof, Time qualifies the spark and fire of it. There lives within the very flame of love A kind of wick or snuff that will abate it, And nothing is at a like goodness still; For goodness, growing to a pleurisy, Dies in his own too-much. That we would do We should do when we would; for this “would” changes And hath abatements and delays as many As there are tongues, are hands, are accidents; And then this “should” is like a spendthrift sigh, That hurts by easing. But to the quick of th’ ulcer: Hamlet comes back; what would you undertake To show yourself indeed your father’s son More than in words?

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: To cut his throat i’ th’ church.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: No place indeed should murder sanctuarize; Revenge should have no bounds. But, good Laertes, Will you do this? Keep close within your chamber. Hamlet, returned, shall know you are come home. We’ll put on those shall praise your excellence And set a double varnish on the fame The Frenchman gave you; bring you, in fine, together And wager on your heads. He, being remiss, Most generous, and free from all contriving, Will not peruse the foils, so that with ease, Or with a little shuffling, you may choose A sword unbated, and in a pass of practice Requite him for your father.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: I will do ’t, And for that purpose I’ll anoint my sword. I bought an unction of a mountebank So mortal that, but dip a knife in it, Where it draws blood no cataplasm so rare, Collected from all simples that have virtue Under the moon, can save the thing from death That is but scratched withal. I’ll touch my point With this contagion, that, if I gall him slightly, It may be death.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Let’s further think of this, Weigh what convenience both of time and means May fit us to our shape. If this should fail, And that our drift look through our bad performance, ’Twere better not assayed. Therefore this project Should have a back or second that might hold If this did blast in proof. Soft, let me see. We’ll make a solemn wager on your cunnings— I ha ’t! When in your motion you are hot and dry (As make your bouts more violent to that end) And that he calls for drink, I’ll have prepared him A chalice for the nonce, whereon but sipping, If he by chance escape your venomed stuck, Our purpose may hold there.—But stay, what noise?

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: One woe doth tread upon another’s heel, So fast they follow. Your sister’s drowned, Laertes.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Drowned? O, where?

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: There is a willow grows askant the brook That shows his hoar leaves in the glassy stream. Therewith fantastic garlands did she make Of crowflowers, nettles, daisies, and long purples, That liberal shepherds give a grosser name, But our cold maids do “dead men’s fingers” call them. There on the pendant boughs her coronet weeds Clamb’ring to hang, an envious sliver broke, When down her weedy trophies and herself Fell in the weeping brook. Her clothes spread wide, And mermaid-like awhile they bore her up, Which time she chanted snatches of old lauds, As one incapable of her own distress Or like a creature native and endued Unto that element. But long it could not be Till that her garments, heavy with their drink, Pulled the poor wretch from her melodious lay To muddy death.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Alas, then she is drowned.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: Drowned, drowned.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Too much of water hast thou, poor Ophelia, And therefore I forbid my tears. But yet It is our trick; nature her custom holds, Let shame say what it will. When these are gone, The woman will be out.—Adieu, my lord. I have a speech o’ fire that fain would blaze, But that this folly drowns it.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Let’s follow, Gertrude. How much I had to do to calm his rage! Now fear I this will give it start again. Therefore, let’s follow.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Is she to be buried in Christian burial, when she willfully seeks her own salvation?

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: I tell thee she is. Therefore make her grave straight. The crowner hath sat on her and finds it Christian burial.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: How can that be, unless she drowned herself in her own defense?

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Why, ’tis found so.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: It must be se offendendo; it cannot be else. For here lies the point: if I drown myself wittingly, it argues an act, and an act hath three branches—it is to act, to do, to perform. Argal, she drowned herself wittingly.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Nay, but hear you, goodman delver—

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Give me leave. Here lies the water; good. Here stands the man; good. If the man go to this water and drown himself, it is (will he, nill he) he goes; mark you that. But if the water come to him and drown him, he drowns not himself. Argal, he that is not guilty of his own death shortens not his own life.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: But is this law?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Ay, marry, is ’t—crowner’s ’quest law.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Will you ha’ the truth on ’t? If this had not been a gentlewoman, she should have been buried out o’ Christian burial.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Why, there thou sayst. And the more pity that great folk should have count’nance in this world to drown or hang themselves more than their even-Christian. Come, my spade. There is no ancient gentlemen but gard’ners, ditchers, and grave-makers. They hold up Adam’s profession.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Was he a gentleman?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: He was the first that ever bore arms.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Why, he had none.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: What, art a heathen? How dost thou understand the scripture? The scripture says Adam digged. Could he dig without arms? I’ll put another question to thee. If thou answerest me not to the purpose, confess thyself—

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Go to!

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: What is he that builds stronger than either the mason, the shipwright, or the carpenter?

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: The gallows-maker; for that frame outlives a thousand tenants.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: I like thy wit well, in good faith. The gallows does well. But how does it well? It does well to those that do ill. Now, thou dost ill to say the gallows is built stronger than the church. Argal, the gallows may do well to thee. To ’t again, come.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: “Who builds stronger than a mason, a shipwright, or a carpenter?”

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Ay, tell me that, and unyoke.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Marry, now I can tell.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: To ’t.

speeches.speaker: OTHER
speeches.text: Mass, I cannot tell.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Cudgel thy brains no more about it, for your dull ass will not mend his pace with beating. And, when you are asked this question next, say “a grave-maker.” The houses he makes lasts till doomsday. Go, get thee in, and fetch me a stoup of liquor. In youth when I did love, did love, Methought it was very sweet To contract—O—the time for—a—my behove, O, methought there—a—was nothing—a—meet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Has this fellow no feeling of his business? He sings in grave-making.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Custom hath made it in him a property of easiness.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: ’Tis e’en so. The hand of little employment hath the daintier sense.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: But age with his stealing steps Hath clawed me in his clutch, And hath shipped me into the land, As if I had never been such.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: That skull had a tongue in it and could sing once. How the knave jowls it to the ground as if ’twere Cain’s jawbone, that did the first murder! This might be the pate of a politician which this ass now o’erreaches, one that would circumvent God, might it not?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: It might, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Or of a courtier, which could say “Good morrow, sweet lord! How dost thou, sweet lord?” This might be my Lord Such-a-one that praised my Lord Such-a-one’s horse when he went to beg it, might it not?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Ay, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why, e’en so. And now my Lady Worm’s, chapless and knocked about the mazard with a sexton’s spade. Here’s fine revolution, an we had the trick to see ’t. Did these bones cost no more the breeding but to play at loggets with them? Mine ache to think on ’t.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: A pickax and a spade, a spade, For and a shrouding sheet, O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: There’s another. Why may not that be the skull of a lawyer? Where be his quiddities now, his quillities, his cases, his tenures, and his tricks? Why does he suffer this mad knave now to knock him about the sconce with a dirty shovel and will not tell him of his action of battery? Hum, this fellow might be in ’s time a great buyer of land, with his statutes, his recognizances, his fines, his double vouchers, his recoveries. Is this the fine of his fines and the recovery of his recoveries, to have his fine pate full of fine dirt? Will his vouchers vouch him no more of his purchases, and double ones too, than the length and breadth of a pair of indentures? The very conveyances of his lands will scarcely lie in this box, and must th’ inheritor himself have no more, ha?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Not a jot more, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Is not parchment made of sheepskins?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Ay, my lord, and of calves’ skins too.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: They are sheep and calves which seek out assurance in that. I will speak to this fellow.— Whose grave’s this, sirrah?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Mine, sir. O, a pit of clay for to be made For such a guest is meet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I think it be thine indeed, for thou liest in ’t.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: You lie out on ’t, sir, and therefore ’tis not yours. For my part, I do not lie in ’t, yet it is mine.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Thou dost lie in ’t, to be in ’t and say it is thine. ’Tis for the dead, not for the quick; therefore thou liest.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: ’Tis a quick lie, sir; ’twill away again from me to you.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What man dost thou dig it for?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: For no man, sir.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What woman then?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: For none, neither.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Who is to be buried in ’t?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: One that was a woman, sir, but, rest her soul, she’s dead.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How absolute the knave is! We must speak by the card, or equivocation will undo us. By the Lord, Horatio, this three years I have took note of it: the age is grown so picked that the toe of the peasant comes so near the heel of the courtier, he galls his kibe.—How long hast thou been grave-maker?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Of all the days i’ th’ year, I came to ’t that day that our last King Hamlet overcame Fortinbras.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How long is that since?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Cannot you tell that? Every fool can tell that. It was that very day that young Hamlet was born—he that is mad, and sent into England.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Ay, marry, why was he sent into England?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Why, because he was mad. He shall recover his wits there. Or if he do not, ’tis no great matter there.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: ’Twill not be seen in him there. There the men are as mad as he.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How came he mad?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Very strangely, they say.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How “strangely”?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Faith, e’en with losing his wits.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Upon what ground?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Why, here in Denmark. I have been sexton here, man and boy, thirty years.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How long will a man lie i’ th’ earth ere he rot?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Faith, if he be not rotten before he die (as we have many pocky corses nowadays that will scarce hold the laying in), he will last you some eight year or nine year. A tanner will last you nine year.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why he more than another?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: Why, sir, his hide is so tanned with his trade that he will keep out water a great while; and your water is a sore decayer of your whoreson dead body. Here’s a skull now hath lien you i’ th’ earth three-and-twenty years.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Whose was it?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: A whoreson mad fellow’s it was. Whose do you think it was?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Nay, I know not.

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: A pestilence on him for a mad rogue! He poured a flagon of Rhenish on my head once. This same skull, sir, was, sir, Yorick’s skull, the King’s jester.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: This?

speeches.speaker: GRAVEDIGGER
speeches.text: E’en that.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Let me see. Alas, poor Yorick! I knew him, Horatio—a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy. He hath bore me on his back a thousand times, and now how abhorred in my imagination it is! My gorge rises at it. Here hung those lips that I have kissed I know not how oft. Where be your gibes now? your gambols? your songs? your flashes of merriment that were wont to set the table on a roar? Not one now to mock your own grinning? Quite chapfallen? Now get you to my lady’s chamber, and tell her, let her paint an inch thick, to this favor she must come. Make her laugh at that.—Prithee, Horatio, tell me one thing.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: What’s that, my lord?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Dost thou think Alexander looked o’ this fashion i’ th’ earth?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: E’en so.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: And smelt so? Pah!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: E’en so, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: To what base uses we may return, Horatio! Why may not imagination trace the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bunghole?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: ’Twere to consider too curiously to consider so.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: No, faith, not a jot; but to follow him thither, with modesty enough and likelihood to lead it, as thus: Alexander died, Alexander was buried, Alexander returneth to dust; the dust is earth; of earth we make loam; and why of that loam whereto he was converted might they not stop a beer barrel? Imperious Caesar, dead and turned to clay, Might stop a hole to keep the wind away. O, that that earth which kept the world in awe Should patch a wall t’ expel the winter’s flaw! But soft, but soft awhile! Here comes the King, The Queen, the courtiers. Who is this they follow? And with such maimèd rites? This doth betoken The corse they follow did with desp’rate hand Fordo its own life. ’Twas of some estate. Couch we awhile and mark.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: What ceremony else?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: That is Laertes, a very noble youth. Mark.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: What ceremony else?

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: Her obsequies have been as far enlarged As we have warranty. Her death was doubtful, And, but that great command o’ersways the order, She should in ground unsanctified been lodged Till the last trumpet. For charitable prayers Shards, flints, and pebbles should be thrown on her. Yet here she is allowed her virgin crants, Her maiden strewments, and the bringing home Of bell and burial.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Must there no more be done?

speeches.speaker: DOCTOR
speeches.text: No more be done. We should profane the service of the dead To sing a requiem and such rest to her As to peace-parted souls.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Lay her i’ th’ earth, And from her fair and unpolluted flesh May violets spring! I tell thee, churlish priest, A minist’ring angel shall my sister be When thou liest howling.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What, the fair Ophelia?

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: Sweets to the sweet, farewell! I hoped thou shouldst have been my Hamlet’s wife; I thought thy bride-bed to have decked, sweet maid, And not have strewed thy grave.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: O, treble woe Fall ten times treble on that cursèd head Whose wicked deed thy most ingenious sense Deprived thee of!—Hold off the earth awhile, Till I have caught her once more in mine arms. Now pile your dust upon the quick and dead, Till of this flat a mountain you have made T’ o’ertop old Pelion or the skyish head Of blue Olympus.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What is he whose grief Bears such an emphasis, whose phrase of sorrow Conjures the wand’ring stars and makes them stand Like wonder-wounded hearers? This is I, Hamlet the Dane.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: The devil take thy soul!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Thou pray’st not well. I prithee take thy fingers from my throat, For though I am not splenitive and rash, Yet have I in me something dangerous, Which let thy wisdom fear. Hold off thy hand.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Pluck them asunder.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: Hamlet! Hamlet!

speeches.speaker: ALL
speeches.text: Gentlemen!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Good my lord, be quiet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why, I will fight with him upon this theme Until my eyelids will no longer wag!

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: O my son, what theme?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I loved Ophelia. Forty thousand brothers Could not with all their quantity of love Make up my sum. What wilt thou do for her?

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: O, he is mad, Laertes!

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: For love of God, forbear him.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: ’Swounds, show me what thou ’t do. Woo’t weep, woo’t fight, woo’t fast, woo’t tear thyself, Woo’t drink up eisel, eat a crocodile? I’ll do ’t. Dost thou come here to whine? To outface me with leaping in her grave? Be buried quick with her, and so will I. And if thou prate of mountains, let them throw Millions of acres on us, till our ground, Singeing his pate against the burning zone, Make Ossa like a wart. Nay, an thou ’lt mouth, I’ll rant as well as thou.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: This is mere madness; And thus awhile the fit will work on him. Anon, as patient as the female dove When that her golden couplets are disclosed, His silence will sit drooping.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Hear you, sir, What is the reason that you use me thus? I loved you ever. But it is no matter. Let Hercules himself do what he may, The cat will mew, and dog will have his day.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: I pray thee, good Horatio, wait upon him. Strengthen your patience in our last night’s speech. We’ll put the matter to the present push.— Good Gertrude, set some watch over your son.— This grave shall have a living monument. An hour of quiet thereby shall we see. Till then in patience our proceeding be.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: So much for this, sir. Now shall you see the other. You do remember all the circumstance?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Remember it, my lord!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Sir, in my heart there was a kind of fighting That would not let me sleep. Methought I lay Worse than the mutines in the bilboes. Rashly— And praised be rashness for it; let us know, Our indiscretion sometime serves us well When our deep plots do pall; and that should learn us There’s a divinity that shapes our ends, Rough-hew them how we will—

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: That is most certain.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Up from my cabin, My sea-gown scarfed about me, in the dark Groped I to find out them; had my desire, Fingered their packet, and in fine withdrew To mine own room again, making so bold (My fears forgetting manners) to unfold Their grand commission; where I found, Horatio, A royal knavery—an exact command, Larded with many several sorts of reasons Importing Denmark’s health and England’s too, With—ho!—such bugs and goblins in my life, That on the supervise, no leisure bated, No, not to stay the grinding of the ax, My head should be struck off.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Is ’t possible?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Here’s the commission. Read it at more leisure. But wilt thou hear now how I did proceed?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: I beseech you.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Being thus benetted round with villainies, Or I could make a prologue to my brains, They had begun the play. I sat me down, Devised a new commission, wrote it fair— I once did hold it, as our statists do, A baseness to write fair, and labored much How to forget that learning; but, sir, now It did me yeoman’s service. Wilt thou know Th’ effect of what I wrote?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Ay, good my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: An earnest conjuration from the King, As England was his faithful tributary, As love between them like the palm might flourish, As peace should still her wheaten garland wear And stand a comma ’tween their amities, And many suchlike of great charge, That, on the view and knowing of these contents, Without debatement further, more or less, He should those bearers put to sudden death, Not shriving time allowed.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: How was this sealed?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why, even in that was heaven ordinant. I had my father’s signet in my purse, Which was the model of that Danish seal; Folded the writ up in the form of th’ other, Subscribed it, gave ’t th’ impression, placed it safely, The changeling never known. Now, the next day Was our sea-fight; and what to this was sequent Thou knowest already.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: So Guildenstern and Rosencrantz go to ’t.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Why, man, they did make love to this employment. They are not near my conscience. Their defeat Does by their own insinuation grow. ’Tis dangerous when the baser nature comes Between the pass and fell incensèd points Of mighty opposites.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Why, what a king is this!

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Does it not, think thee, stand me now upon— He that hath killed my king and whored my mother, Popped in between th’ election and my hopes, Thrown out his angle for my proper life, And with such cozenage—is ’t not perfect conscience To quit him with this arm? And is ’t not to be damned To let this canker of our nature come In further evil?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: It must be shortly known to him from England What is the issue of the business there.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: It will be short. The interim’s mine, And a man’s life’s no more than to say “one.” But I am very sorry, good Horatio, That to Laertes I forgot myself, For by the image of my cause I see The portraiture of his. I’ll court his favors. But, sure, the bravery of his grief did put me Into a tow’ring passion.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Peace, who comes here?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Your Lordship is right welcome back to Denmark.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I humbly thank you, sir. Dost know this waterfly?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: No, my good lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Thy state is the more gracious, for ’tis a vice to know him. He hath much land, and fertile. Let a beast be lord of beasts and his crib shall stand at the king’s mess. ’Tis a chough, but, as I say, spacious in the possession of dirt.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Sweet lord, if your Lordship were at leisure, I should impart a thing to you from his Majesty.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I will receive it, sir, with all diligence of spirit. Put your bonnet to his right use: ’tis for the head.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: I thank your Lordship; it is very hot.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: No, believe me, ’tis very cold; the wind is northerly.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: It is indifferent cold, my lord, indeed.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: But yet methinks it is very sultry and hot for my complexion.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Exceedingly, my lord; it is very sultry, as ’twere—I cannot tell how. My lord, his Majesty bade me signify to you that he has laid a great wager on your head. Sir, this is the matter—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I beseech you, remember.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Nay, good my lord, for my ease, in good faith. Sir, here is newly come to court Laertes—believe me, an absolute gentleman, full of most excellent differences, of very soft society and great showing. Indeed, to speak feelingly of him, he is the card or calendar of gentry, for you shall find in him the continent of what part a gentleman would see.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Sir, his definement suffers no perdition in you, though I know to divide him inventorially would dozy th’ arithmetic of memory, and yet but yaw neither, in respect of his quick sail. But, in the verity of extolment, I take him to be a soul of great article, and his infusion of such dearth and rareness as, to make true diction of him, his semblable is his mirror, and who else would trace him, his umbrage, nothing more.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Your Lordship speaks most infallibly of him.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: The concernancy, sir? Why do we wrap the gentleman in our more rawer breath?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Sir?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Is ’t not possible to understand in another tongue? You will to ’t, sir, really.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What imports the nomination of this gentleman?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Of Laertes?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: His purse is empty already; all ’s golden words are spent.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Of him, sir.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: I know you are not ignorant—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I would you did, sir. Yet, in faith, if you did, it would not much approve me. Well, sir?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: You are not ignorant of what excellence Laertes is—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I dare not confess that, lest I should compare with him in excellence. But to know a man well were to know himself.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: I mean, sir, for his weapon. But in the imputation laid on him by them, in his meed he’s unfellowed.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What’s his weapon?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Rapier and dagger.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: That’s two of his weapons. But, well—

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: The King, sir, hath wagered with him six Barbary horses, against the which he has impawned, as I take it, six French rapiers and poniards, with their assigns, as girdle, hangers, and so. Three of the carriages, in faith, are very dear to fancy, very responsive to the hilts, most delicate carriages, and of very liberal conceit.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: What call you the “carriages”?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: I knew you must be edified by the margent ere you had done.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: The carriages, sir, are the hangers.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: The phrase would be more germane to the matter if we could carry a cannon by our sides. I would it might be “hangers” till then. But on. Six Barbary horses against six French swords, their assigns, and three liberal-conceited carriages— that’s the French bet against the Danish. Why is this all “impawned,” as you call it?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: The King, sir, hath laid, sir, that in a dozen passes between yourself and him, he shall not exceed you three hits. He hath laid on twelve for nine, and it would come to immediate trial if your Lordship would vouchsafe the answer.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How if I answer no?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: I mean, my lord, the opposition of your person in trial.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Sir, I will walk here in the hall. If it please his Majesty, it is the breathing time of day with me. Let the foils be brought, the gentleman willing, and the King hold his purpose, I will win for him, an I can. If not, I will gain nothing but my shame and the odd hits.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Shall I deliver you e’en so?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: To this effect, sir, after what flourish your nature will.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: I commend my duty to your Lordship.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Yours. He does well to commend it himself. There are no tongues else for ’s turn.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: This lapwing runs away with the shell on his head.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: He did comply, sir, with his dug before he sucked it. Thus has he (and many more of the same breed that I know the drossy age dotes on) only got the tune of the time, and, out of an habit of encounter, a kind of yeasty collection, which carries them through and through the most fanned and winnowed opinions; and do but blow them to their trial, the bubbles are out.

speeches.speaker: LORD
speeches.text: My lord, his Majesty commended him to you by young Osric, who brings back to him that you attend him in the hall. He sends to know if your pleasure hold to play with Laertes, or that you will take longer time.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I am constant to my purposes. They follow the King’s pleasure. If his fitness speaks, mine is ready now or whensoever, provided I be so able as now.

speeches.speaker: LORD
speeches.text: The King and Queen and all are coming down.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: In happy time.

speeches.speaker: LORD
speeches.text: The Queen desires you to use some gentle entertainment to Laertes before you fall to play.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: She well instructs me.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: You will lose, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I do not think so. Since he went into France, I have been in continual practice. I shall win at the odds; but thou wouldst not think how ill all’s here about my heart. But it is no matter.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Nay, good my lord—

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: It is but foolery, but it is such a kind of gaingiving as would perhaps trouble a woman.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: If your mind dislike anything, obey it. I will forestall their repair hither and say you are not fit.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Not a whit. We defy augury. There is a special providence in the fall of a sparrow. If it be now, ’tis not to come; if it be not to come, it will be now; if it be not now, yet it will come. The readiness is all. Since no man of aught he leaves knows, what is ’t to leave betimes? Let be.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Come, Hamlet, come and take this hand from me.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Give me your pardon, sir. I have done you wrong; But pardon ’t as you are a gentleman. This presence knows, And you must needs have heard, how I am punished With a sore distraction. What I have done That might your nature, honor, and exception Roughly awake, I here proclaim was madness. Was ’t Hamlet wronged Laertes? Never Hamlet. If Hamlet from himself be ta’en away, And when he’s not himself does wrong Laertes, Then Hamlet does it not; Hamlet denies it. Who does it, then? His madness. If ’t be so, Hamlet is of the faction that is wronged; His madness is poor Hamlet’s enemy. Sir, in this audience Let my disclaiming from a purposed evil Free me so far in your most generous thoughts That I have shot my arrow o’er the house And hurt my brother.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: I am satisfied in nature, Whose motive in this case should stir me most To my revenge; but in my terms of honor I stand aloof and will no reconcilement Till by some elder masters of known honor I have a voice and precedent of peace To keep my name ungored. But till that time I do receive your offered love like love And will not wrong it.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I embrace it freely And will this brothers’ wager frankly play.— Give us the foils. Come on.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Come, one for me.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I’ll be your foil, Laertes; in mine ignorance Your skill shall, like a star i’ th’ darkest night, Stick fiery off indeed.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: You mock me, sir.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: No, by this hand.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Give them the foils, young Osric. Cousin Hamlet, You know the wager?

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Very well, my lord. Your Grace has laid the odds o’ th’ weaker side.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: I do not fear it; I have seen you both. But, since he is better, we have therefore odds.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: This is too heavy. Let me see another.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: This likes me well. These foils have all a length?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Ay, my good lord.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Set me the stoups of wine upon that table.— If Hamlet give the first or second hit Or quit in answer of the third exchange, Let all the battlements their ordnance fire. The King shall drink to Hamlet’s better breath, And in the cup an union shall he throw, Richer than that which four successive kings In Denmark’s crown have worn. Give me the cups, And let the kettle to the trumpet speak, The trumpet to the cannoneer without, The cannons to the heavens, the heaven to earth, “Now the King drinks to Hamlet.” Come, begin. And you, the judges, bear a wary eye.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Come on, sir.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Come, my lord.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: One.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: No.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Judgment!

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: A hit, a very palpable hit.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Well, again.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Stay, give me drink.—Hamlet, this pearl is thine. Here’s to thy health. Give him the cup.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I’ll play this bout first. Set it by awhile. Come. Another hit. What say you?

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: A touch, a touch. I do confess ’t.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Our son shall win.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: He’s fat and scant of breath.— Here, Hamlet, take my napkin; rub thy brows. The Queen carouses to thy fortune, Hamlet.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Good madam.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Gertrude, do not drink.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: I will, my lord; I pray you pardon me.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: It is the poisoned cup. It is too late.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: I dare not drink yet, madam—by and by.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: Come, let me wipe thy face.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: My lord, I’ll hit him now.

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: I do not think ’t.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: And yet it is almost against my conscience.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Come, for the third, Laertes. You do but dally. I pray you pass with your best violence. I am afeard you make a wanton of me.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Say you so? Come on.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Nothing neither way.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Have at you now!

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: Part them. They are incensed.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Nay, come again.

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Look to the Queen there, ho!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: They bleed on both sides.—How is it, my lord?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: How is ’t, Laertes?

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: Why as a woodcock to mine own springe, Osric. I am justly killed with mine own treachery.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: How does the Queen?

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: She swoons to see them bleed.

speeches.speaker: QUEEN
speeches.text: No, no, the drink, the drink! O, my dear Hamlet! The drink, the drink! I am poisoned.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: O villainy! Ho! Let the door be locked. Treachery! Seek it out.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: It is here, Hamlet. Hamlet, thou art slain. No med’cine in the world can do thee good. In thee there is not half an hour’s life. The treacherous instrument is in thy hand, Unbated and envenomed. The foul practice Hath turned itself on me. Lo, here I lie, Never to rise again. Thy mother’s poisoned. I can no more. The King, the King’s to blame.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: The point envenomed too! Then, venom, to thy work.

speeches.speaker: ALL
speeches.text: Treason, treason!

speeches.speaker: KING
speeches.text: O, yet defend me, friends! I am but hurt.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Here, thou incestuous, murd’rous, damnèd Dane, Drink off this potion. Is thy union here? Follow my mother.

speeches.speaker: LAERTES
speeches.text: He is justly served. It is a poison tempered by himself. Exchange forgiveness with me, noble Hamlet. Mine and my father’s death come not upon thee, Nor thine on me.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: Heaven make thee free of it. I follow thee.— I am dead, Horatio.—Wretched queen, adieu.— You that look pale and tremble at this chance, That are but mutes or audience to this act, Had I but time (as this fell sergeant, Death, Is strict in his arrest), O, I could tell you— But let it be.—Horatio, I am dead. Thou livest; report me and my cause aright To the unsatisfied.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Never believe it. I am more an antique Roman than a Dane. Here’s yet some liquor left.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: As thou ’rt a man, Give me the cup. Let go! By heaven, I’ll ha ’t. O God, Horatio, what a wounded name, Things standing thus unknown, shall I leave behind me! If thou didst ever hold me in thy heart, Absent thee from felicity awhile And in this harsh world draw thy breath in pain To tell my story. What warlike noise is this?

speeches.speaker: OSRIC
speeches.text: Young Fortinbras, with conquest come from Poland, To th’ ambassadors of England gives This warlike volley.

speeches.speaker: HAMLET
speeches.text: O, I die, Horatio! The potent poison quite o’ercrows my spirit. I cannot live to hear the news from England. But I do prophesy th’ election lights On Fortinbras; he has my dying voice. So tell him, with th’ occurrents, more and less, Which have solicited—the rest is silence. O, O, O, O!

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest. Why does the drum come hither?

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
speeches.text: Where is this sight?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: What is it you would see? If aught of woe or wonder, cease your search.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
speeches.text: This quarry cries on havoc. O proud Death, What feast is toward in thine eternal cell That thou so many princes at a shot So bloodily hast struck?

speeches.speaker: AMBASSADOR
speeches.text: The sight is dismal, And our affairs from England come too late. The ears are senseless that should give us hearing To tell him his commandment is fulfilled, That Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are dead. Where should we have our thanks?

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Not from his mouth, Had it th’ ability of life to thank you. He never gave commandment for their death. But since, so jump upon this bloody question, You from the Polack wars, and you from England, Are here arrived, give order that these bodies High on a stage be placed to the view, And let me speak to th’ yet unknowing world How these things came about. So shall you hear Of carnal, bloody, and unnatural acts, Of accidental judgments, casual slaughters, Of deaths put on by cunning and forced cause, And, in this upshot, purposes mistook Fall’n on th’ inventors’ heads. All this can I Truly deliver.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
speeches.text: Let us haste to hear it And call the noblest to the audience. For me, with sorrow I embrace my fortune. I have some rights of memory in this kingdom, Which now to claim my vantage doth invite me.

speeches.speaker: HORATIO
speeches.text: Of that I shall have also cause to speak, And from his mouth whose voice will draw on more. But let this same be presently performed Even while men’s minds are wild, lest more mischance On plots and errors happen.

speeches.speaker: FORTINBRAS
speeches.text: Let four captains Bear Hamlet like a soldier to the stage, For he was likely, had he been put on, To have proved most royal; and for his passage, The soldier’s music and the rite of war Speak loudly for him. Take up the bodies. Such a sight as this Becomes the field but here shows much amiss. Go, bid the soldiers shoot.
